Project Overview & Iterative Evolution (Week 2 Refinements + Week 3 Advanced Modeling)¶

Following the strategic planning established in Week 1 (Problem Formulation) and initial technical execution in Week 2 (Data Preparation, Baseline Modeling & EDA), this notebook advances the FinTrust Digital Banking Risk Review project into a complete, technically robust, and production-ready predictive solution.

In accordance with mentor evaluation feedback on Week 2, this notebook incorporates 5 critical technical refinements in data preparation, feature engineering, and validation methodology prior to deploying advanced classification architectures (XGBoost, LightGBM, and tuned Ensembles).

Key Technical Refinements Implemented (Based on Mentor Feedback)¶

To eliminate methodological weaknesses and data leakage present in the initial baseline, the following adjustments have been applied:

  1. Data Leakage Elimination in Feature Engineering: Customer-level historical metrics (e.g., Customer_Tx_Count, customer_avg_amount, Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio) are now computed cumulatively and chronologically using only historical transactions prior to the prediction timestamp (shift(1) expanding windows), preventing future transaction information from leaking into training features
  2. Correction of Temporal Logic (Is_Weekend_Transaction): Corrected the weekend logic operator from dayofweek > 5 (which previously captured Sunday only) to dayofweek >= 5 (capturing both Saturday [5] and Sunday [6])
  3. Explicit Outlier Treatment: Replaced implicit scaling-only handling with an explicit Interquartile Range (IQR) capping/winsorization analysis on Amount_NGN to handle extreme transaction values cleanly without dropping informative tail signals
  4. Time-Aware Validation Strategy: Transitioned from a purely randomized stratified split to a Time-Based Chronological Train/Test Split (80/20), respecting real-world banking sequence order where models train on historical transactions to predict future incoming events
  5. Target Leakage Review (Transaction_Status): Evaluated real-time availability of post-execution status fields and removed potential target leakage variables prior to scoring.

Week 3 Objectives & Deliverables Covered in this Notebook¶

This notebook executes the Week 3 scope in two distinct operational phases:

Phase 1: Week 2 Refinement & Methodological Improvements (Part A — Review Baseline & Data Prep)¶

  • Chronological Data Sorting & Percentage Fixes: Sorted the merged dataset chronologically by Transaction_DateTime and updated missingness calculations to explicit percentage formulas (* 100)
  • Explicit Outlier Treatment: Implemented an Interquartile Range (IQR) capping/winsorization protocol on Amount_NGN to handle extreme monetary values without dropping informative tail signals
  • Data Leakage Elimination: Re-engineered customer-level metrics (Customer_Tx_Count, customer_avg_amount, Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio) using strictly historical, time-ordered cumulative windows (shift(1) expanding means) to prevent future information leakage.
  • Temporal Logic Correction: Corrected Is_Weekend_Transaction logic from dayofweek > 5 to dayofweek >= 5 to accurately capture both Saturday and Sunday operations
  • Time-Aware Baseline Re-evaluation: Transitioned to an 80/20 Chronological Validation Split and re-evaluated Logistic Regression and Random Forest baseline models under time-series conditions.

Phase 2: Week 3 Advanced Modeling, Validation & Candidate Selection (Parts B to G)¶

  1. Part B — Develop Additional Models: Trained sequential gradient boosting architectures (XGBoost and LightGBM) with native class imbalance handling (scale_pos_weight) and probability threshold tuning
  2. Part C — Feature Refinement: Documented a formal Feature Refinement Decision Table to eliminate target leakage (removing Transaction_Status) and control feature space dimensionality
  3. Part D — Model Comparison: Evaluated and compared all 4 trained models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) across Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and PR-AUC
  4. Part E — Error Analysis: Conducted an in-depth investigation of False Positives (customer friction and operational review queue burden) versus False Negatives (unmitigated financial exposure)
  5. Part F — Model Interpretation: Evaluated global feature drivers and decision boundaries using Permutation Importance on the time-split test set
  6. Part G — Candidate Final Model Selection: Selected and formally documented the candidate model (Random Forest Classifier) to carry forward into Week 4 for final testing, optimization, and integration.

Summary of Data Preparation Actions - Part A¶

  1. Data Ingestion and Merging: Both customer and transaction datasets were successfully loaded and merged via an inner join on Customer_ID. The merged dataset captures complete transactional records enriched with customer demographic attributes
  2. Missing Value Strategy: Missing values identified in categorical fields such as Device_Type and Location will not be dropped to prevent data loss. Instead, missing entries will be explicitly categorized as "Missing/Unknown" during preprocessing to retain potentially informative missingness signals
  3. Duplicate Verification: Confirmed zero duplicate records across the merged dataset, establishing data integrity
  4. Data Type Adjustments: Raw date/time attributes (Transaction_DateTime) were identified as needing datetime casting to enable engineered temporal features in subsequent phases
  5. Unusual Values Assessment: Descriptive statistics confirmed valid bounds across numerical features (Amount_NGN, Monthly_Income_Band, Tenure_Months). No unphysical or negative values were present; high-value skewness in transaction amounts will be addressed using robust scaling

  7. Variable Exclusion Rationale: Primary key identifiers (Transaction_ID, Customer_ID) are excluded from predictive features to prevent overfitting and target leakage. Raw timestamps will be transformed into structured features prior to model fitting

Part C — Feature Engineering¶

Following the exploratory data analysis and hypothesis testing in Part B, we proceed with feature engineering to transform raw fields into domain-relevant predictive indicators. Our objective is to engineer high-signal composite variables while controlling dimensionality and strictly incorporating recommendations from AnalystLab.

Key feature construction strategies include:

  1. Transaction Velocity & Frequency: Computing total customer transactions (Customer_Tx_Count) and monthly activity velocity (Transaction_Frequency)
  2. Transaction Amount Segmentation: Discretizing transaction values into statistical quartiles (Amount_Category)
  3. Targeted Account Risk ($H_3$): Combining short account tenure (Tenure_Months) with high-value transactions (New_Account_High_Risk)
  4. Cross-Border Interactions ($H_4$): Capturing the strong interaction effect between execution channels (Channel) and international status (International_Transaction)
  5. Security & Metadata Anomaly Flags ($H_2$): Isolating unknown device types (Is_Unverified_Device) and unknown location metadata (Location_Mismatch_Flag)
  6. Temporal Indicators: Extracting time components (Transaction_DateTime), night-time anomalies (Is_Night_Transaction), and digital engagement bands

Feature Engineering Documentation Table (Leak-Free & Time-Aware Pipeline)¶

A total of 16 predictive features were engineered based on the updated leak-free feature engineering pipeline, addressing all mentor observations regarding temporal logic, data integrity, and leakage prevention.

Feature Name How It Was Created Why It Matters & Leak-Free Rationale
Amount_Category Quantile binning (pd.qcut) of Amount_NGN into four equal tiers Discretizes continuous transaction amounts into quantile-based risk bands to capture non-linear risk spikes
Transaction_Frequency Calculated as Customer_Tx_Count / (Tenure_Months + 1) Captures monthly transaction velocity based strictly on past account usage patterns
Is_Unverified_Device Binary flag (1/0) active when Device_Type == 'Unknown' Isolates untracked or unverified access endpoints for risk screening
Location_Mismatch_Flag Binary flag (1/0) active when Location == 'Unknown' Flags missing origin metadata and untracked geographic execution points
Digital_Engagement_Category Binned Digital_Engagement_Score using pd.cut into Low, Medium, High tiers Discretizes user engagement levels to capture non-linear adoption behaviors
Transaction_Hour Execution hour (0–23) extracted from Transaction_DateTime.dt.hour Identifies time-of-day execution distributions to isolate off-hour risk patterns
Transaction_Day Day of the week (0–6) extracted from Transaction_DateTime.dt.dayofweek Distinguishes weekday standard operations from weekend activity profiles
Is_Night_Transaction Binary flag (1/0) active for operations executed between 11 PM and 5 AM Off-peak night operations correlate with automated script executions or compromised access
Is_Weekend_Transaction Mentor Fix: Binary flag (1/0) active when Transaction_Day >= 5 (Saturday & Sunday) Corrected Logic: Accurately captures full weekend operations where support capacity is reduced
New_Account_High_Risk Binary flag (1/0) combining short tenure (Tenure_Months <= 6) with above-median amount Targets compound risk profiles where recent accounts perform unexpectedly high-value operations
CrossBorder_Web_Interaction Binary flag (1/0) combining International_Transaction == 'Yes' with Web/ATM/POS channels Leverages interaction effects between international operations and execution access channels
Channel_Mismatch_Flag Binary flag (1/0) active when Channel != Preferred_Channel Detects channel divergence where a user transacts outside historical channel preference
customer_avg_amount Leak-Free: Historical expanding mean of Amount_NGN per customer using .shift(1) Leak-Free: Establishes past personal spending baseline without incorporating future/current amounts
Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio Calculated as Amount_NGN / customer_avg_amount Measures relative spending spikes compared strictly to an individual customer's past baseline
Is_High_Value_Customer_Anomaly Binary flag (1/0) active when Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio > 3.0 Flags extreme spending anomalies exceeding 3x the customer's average historical amount
Is_Suspended_Or_Inactive_Account Binary flag (1/0) active when Account_Status is in Suspended, Inactive, or Closed Flags attempted operations originating from restricted or administratively flagged account states

Part D & E — Baseline Model Development & Evaluation¶

In this section, we build and evaluate a baseline classification model to establish a performance benchmark for transaction risk identification.

1. Baseline Algorithm Choice: Logistic Regression¶

We select Logistic Regression as our baseline model for the following technical reasons:

  • Linear Benchmark: It provides a simple, highly interpretable baseline that evaluates class separability under linear assumptions
  • Calibrated Probabilities: It directly estimates class probabilities, allowing fine-grained threshold tuning for risk screening
  • Class Balance Management: Incorporating class-weight balancing (class_weight='balanced') mitigates the moderate class imbalance (~20% flagged transactions)

2. Data Preparation & Preprocessing¶

  • Feature Selection: Non-predictive identifiers (Transaction_ID, Customer_ID) and timestamps (Transaction_DateTime) are excluded
  • Preprocessing Pipeline: Categorical features are encoded using OneHotEncoder(drop='first'), and continuous numerical features are standardized using StandardScaler()
  • Data Splitting: A 80/20 stratified split (train_test_split(stratify=y)) ensures that class distributions remain consistent across training and test sets

3. Metric Selection Strategy (Part E Rationale)¶

For financial risk screening, metrics carry distinct operational trade-offs:

  • Recall (Sensitivity): Primary metric. False Negatives (unflagged risky transactions) expose the institution to financial loss and compliance penalties
  • Precision: Measures false alarm rates. False Positives create operational overhead during manual reviews
  • F1-Score & PR-AUC: Evaluate global model discrimination and balance between Precision and Recall.

4. Baseline Model Evaluation & Metrics Analysis (Re-evaluated with Time Split & Threshold = 0.57)¶

The baseline Logistic Regression model was re-evaluated under a strict Time-Aware Chronological Validation Split (80/20) with class-weight balancing (class_weight='balanced'). To balance operational workload (False Positives) with risk detection coverage (Recall), the decision threshold was adjusted to 0.57.

Given the skewed test set class distribution (19.25% positive risk prevalence), model performance is evaluated primarily using Precision-Recall metrics and PR-AUC rather than standard ROC-AUC.

4.1. Empirical Performance Summary¶

  • Accuracy: 70.08% — Proportion of correctly classified transactions overall (up from 58.71% at 0.50 threshold)
  • Precision: 31.71% — Proportion of flagged transactions that are truly high-risk (222 True Positives out of 700 total flags generated)
  • Recall: 48.05% — Risk detection coverage (successfully capturing 222 out of 462 actual risk transactions)
  • F1-Score: 0.3821 — Harmonic balance between Precision and Recall
  • PR-AUC: 0.3360 (Average Precision: 0.3375) — Primary evaluation metric for imbalanced data, benchmarked against a 0.1925 (19.25%) random chance prevalence baseline

4.2. Analytical & PR-Curve Interpretation¶

  1. Substantial Lift Over Random Baseline: The PR-AUC of 0.3360 demonstrates an absolute +14.35% lift (+74.5% relative improvement) over the random guess baseline ($y = 0.1925$), confirming that the leak-free engineered features convey genuine predictive signal under time-aware validation

  2. Threshold Optimization Impact (0.57 vs 0.50): Shifting the classification decision threshold from 0.50 to 0.57 successfully reduced False Positives from 839 down to 478. This significantly decreases operational compliance friction and boosts overall classification Accuracy to 70.08%, while preserving a stable F1-Score (0.3821)

  3. Operational Risk Trade-off: The confusion matrix shows 222 True Positives (risk caught) vs. 240 False Negatives (risk missed). While tighter thresholds improve precision and reduce manual investigation queues, linear logistic hyperplanes still exhibit a trade-off limit when trying to isolate complex, non-linear fraud interactions.

4.3. Transition to Advanced Ensemble Modeling¶

The baseline PR-AUC of 0.3360 serves as our leak-free benchmark. Non-linear tree ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) will now be deployed to push the Precision-Recall frontier upward, aiming to improve Precision without sacrificing Recall.

Advanced Model Development — Random Forest Classifier¶

To address the non-linear patterns and complex feature interactions that limited the performance of the baseline Logistic Regression model, we implement a Random Forest Classifier.

Why Random Forest?¶

  • Non-Linear Capability: Captures intricate, non-linear relationships and conditional risk pathways across features without requiring manual transformation.
  • Variance Reduction & Robustness: Aggregates predictions from an ensemble of decision trees (bagging), significantly reducing the risk of overfitting compared to a single decision tree.
  • Imbalance Mitigation: Incorporates class_weight='balanced' to adjust tree split criteria, placing greater weight on correctly identifying high-risk transactions.

Part E — Advanced Model (Random Forest) Evaluation & Critical Assessment¶

1. Performance Overview vs. Baseline¶

Applying automated threshold optimization ($Threshold = 0.4286$) to the Random Forest classifier shifts the operational trade-off significantly toward maximum risk capture compared to the Logistic Regression baseline ($Threshold = 0.57$):

  • Accuracy: 56.67% (vs. 70.08% Baseline) — Lower overall accuracy due to higher false positive volume generated during aggressive risk screening
  • Precision: 26.95% (vs. 31.71% Baseline) — Slight reduction in alarm precision, yielding ~27% true positive rate on flagged transactions
  • Recall: 73.16% (vs. 48.05% Baseline) — +25.11% absolute gain in risk detection, capturing 338 out of 462 actual high-risk transactions
  • F1-Score: 0.3939 (vs. 0.3821 Baseline) — Higher overall balance, driven by the substantial increase in minority class recall
  • PR-AUC: 0.3131 (vs. 0.3360 Baseline) — Slightly lower global precision-recall curve integral under chronological validation split

2. Critical Assessment¶

Strengths¶
  • Superior Risk Detection Coverage: Capturing 73.16% of all fraudulent/risk events significantly reduces the bank's unmitigated financial exposure compared to the linear baseline
  • Non-Linear Feature Interaction Capture: Tree splits successfully leverage complex interactions across continuous spending ratios and time features without requiring linear separability
Limitations¶
  • Increased Operational Review Burden: To achieve 73% recall, false alarms increased, reducing overall Accuracy to 56.67% and requiring higher manual verification capacity
  • Stagnant PR-AUC Ceiling: While Recall improved substantially at threshold 0.4286, the overall PR-AUC curve boundary remains close to the baseline (~0.31–0.33), highlighting the need for sequential boosting algorithms

3. Recommended Next Steps & Algorithm Roadmap¶

To maintain this high Recall (~73%+) while suppressing false alarms and elevating Precision, the following advanced techniques will be executed next:

A. Gradient Boosting Frameworks (XGBoost / LightGBM / CatBoost)¶
  • Deploy XGBoost with scale_pos_weight and focal loss optimization to refine decision boundaries on hard-to-classify border cases.
B. Feature Selection & Post-Hoc Calibration¶
  • Apply SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) feature filtering to prune noisy variables and calibrate predicted probability distributions.

Part F — Initial Model Interpretation & Critical Analysis¶

To understand how our models make decisions, we extract and evaluate the most influential features for both the linear baseline (Logistic Regression) and the non-linear ensemble (Random Forest).

The structured Feature → Evidence → Interpretation framework below outlines our findings, followed by a critical review of model limitations, data constraints, potential biases, and avenues for future investigation.

1. Feature → Evidence → Interpretation Matrix¶

  • Transaction Amount / Ratios:

    • Interpretation: Unusual transaction volumes relative to historical baselines strongly drive the risk score, acting as a primary indicator of potential fraudulent activity
  • Temporal Patterns (Night / Weekend Transactions):
    • Evidence: Moderate positive weights for late-hour operations and weekend activity flags
    • Interpretation: Transactions executed outside normal business hours reflect behavioral anomalies that elevate the probability of a risk review
  • Metadata & Device Verification:
    • Evidence: Unverified device flags and location mismatch indicators show consistent positive weights across both models
    • Interpretation: Missing authentication metadata or operational origin discrepancies significantly compromise transaction trust levels

1. Comparative Feature Influence Analysis¶

Comparing feature behaviors across Logistic Regression and Random Forest after implementing leak-free feature engineering and explicit IQR capping reveals key structural differences in how linear and non-linear models evaluate transaction risk:

  • Top Linear Drivers (Logistic Regression):

    • Transaction_Type_Transfer (+0.6968) and Amount_NGN (+0.3383) dominate positive linear log-odds predictions, serving as primary baseline indicators of elevated financial exposure
    • Amount_NGN_Capped (-0.1242) and Transaction_Hour (-0.1086) act as linear stabilizing offsets against extreme outlier spikes

  • Top Tree-Based Drivers (Random Forest):

    • Continuous numerical features lead Gini split importance: Amount_NGN (9.40%), Transaction_Hour (7.42%), Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio (5.74%), Amount_NGN_Capped (5.61%), and leak-free customer_avg_amount (5.39%)

  • Key Methodological Takeaways:

    • Tree Granularity Preference: Random Forest naturally favors granular continuous variables (Amount_NGN, Transaction_Hour, Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio) due to multiple decision split points across decision trees
    • Validation of Leak-Free Features: Engineered historical customer baselines (customer_avg_amount at 5.39% and Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio at 5.74%) rank among the top 5 most influential features in Random Forest, validating that mentor-requested leak-free features convey strong predictive signal without introducing future information

2. Feature → Evidence → Interpretation Matrix¶

  • Transaction Amount (Amount_NGN / Amount_NGN_Capped):

    • Evidence: Rank #1 in Random Forest (9.40% Gini importance) and high positive linear coefficient (+0.3383) in Logistic Regression
    • Interpretation: Monetary volume remains the single strongest baseline partition signal. Explicit IQR capping successfully preserves this signal while preventing extreme outliers from distorting linear boundary fitting

  • Execution Timing (Transaction_Hour):

    • Evidence: Rank #2 in Random Forest (7.42% Gini importance) and noticeable negative coefficient (-0.1086) in Logistic Regression
    • Interpretation: Temporal execution distributions isolate off-hour operations, serving as a key non-linear behavioral anomaly indicator across decision trees

  • Customer Behavioral Spikes (Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio & customer_avg_amount):

    • Evidence: Near-zero linear weight in Logistic Regression (-0.0019) but high combined tree importance (11.13% total Gini importance across both features)
    • Interpretation: Deviations from individual historical baselines act non-linearly; they become critical flags primarily when combined conditionally with execution channels and timing.

3. Critical Assessment & Project Governance¶

Model Limitations¶
  • Logistic Regression: Constrained by linear decision boundaries, requiring manual cross-term engineering to capture conditional risk interactions
  • Random Forest: Exhibits high feature importance bias toward continuous numerical variables and experiences elevated false alarm volume when optimizing for high recall on imbalanced targets
Data Limitations¶
  • Imbalanced Target Class: High-risk transactions represent a minority (~19.25% in test set), constraining class boundary estimation without advanced boosting loss functions or resampling
  • Lack of Historical Longitudinal Metadata: The dataset lacks multi-month historical chargeback/dispute logs and device fingerprint history.
Possible Sources of Bias¶
  • Synthetic Generation & Artifact Bias: Ground-truth labels reflect predefined algorithmic rules rather than organic human fraud tactics
  • Prior Prevalence Bias: The synthetic risk rate (~19.25%) significantly exceeds real-world banking environments where fraud typically represents less than 1–2% of total transaction volume
  • Deterministic Feature-Label Coupling: Synthetic pipelines often embed rigid heuristics (e.g., heavily weighting Transaction_Type_Transfer), forcing models to learn author-defined rules rather than subtle fraud behavior.
Areas Requiring Further Investigation (Week 3 Advanced Roadmap)¶
  1. Sequential Gradient Boosting (XGBoost / LightGBM / CatBoost): Deploy gradient boosting architectures with scale_pos_weight tuning to refine boundary splits on hard-to-classify risk cases
  2. Post-Hoc Probability Calibration: Apply Platt Scaling or Isotonic Regression to align predicted probability outputs with operational base rates
  3. Model Explainability via SHAP: Utilize SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values to audit feature interactions and confirm that models are learning genuine risk patterns rather than synthetic generation artifacts

Week 3 — Part B: Develop Additional Models (XGBoost & LightGBM)¶

To push beyond the baseline performance boundaries established by Logistic Regression and Random Forest, we deploy two state-of-the-art sequential ensemble architectures: XGBoost (Extreme Gradient Boosting) and LightGBM (Light Gradient Boosting Machine).

Unlike Random Forest's parallel tree construction (Bagging), Gradient Boosting algorithms build decision trees sequentially, where each new tree focuses specifically on minimizing the prediction residuals (errors) of the preceding trees.

Key Modeling Adjustments for Imbalanced Financial Risk:¶

  1. XGBoost Imbalance Control (scale_pos_weight): Set to the ratio of negative to positive training samples (~4.08), heavily penalizing misclassified risk transactions during tree splits
  2. LightGBM Imbalance Control (is_unbalance=True): Automatically adjusts class weights inversely proportional to class frequencies
  3. Automated Threshold Optimization: Probability decision thresholds are tuned automatically on validation predictions to optimize F1-Score and maintain target Recall.

Interpretation & Empirical Findings — Part B (XGBoost & LightGBM vs. Random Forest)¶

Evaluating XGBoost and LightGBM under identical time-aware validation conditions yields important technical insights into algorithm selection for synthetic banking data:

1. Empirical Results Summary¶

  • XGBoost Classifier (Optimal Threshold = 0.4786):
    • Accuracy: 63.04% | Precision: 28.38% | Recall: 60.39% | F1-Score: 0.3862 | PR-AUC: 0.3024
  • LightGBM Classifier (Optimal Threshold = 0.4490):
    • Accuracy: 59.62% | Precision: 27.51% | Recall: 67.10% | F1-Score: 0.3902 | PR-AUC: 0.2967

2. Comparative Analysis & Algorithm Behavior¶

  1. Random Forest Superiority on Minority Recall & PR-AUC: Contrary to theoretical expectations where sequential boosting often outperforms bagging, Random Forest maintains the highest risk coverage (Recall = 73.16%, F1 = 0.3939, PR-AUC = 0.3131) among non-linear models
  2. Impact of Synthetic Data Structure & Bagging Stability: Synthetic financial transaction datasets frequently embed broad, parallel decision boundaries rather than intricate, multi-layered residual structures. Random Forest's variance-reduction via parallel tree averaging (Bagging) proves more resilient to synthetic noise than default sequential gradient boosting
  3. Precision vs. Recall Trade-off: While XGBoost achieves slightly higher overall accuracy (63.04%) and precision (28.38%) by making more conservative predictions, it misses ~40% of risky transactions (Recall = 60.39%). For financial risk screening where unmitigated fraud exposure carries severe penalties, Random Forest's 73.16% risk capture rate remains superior

3. Methodological Takeaway for Candidate Selection¶

This empirical finding validates the "No Free Lunch" theorem in Machine Learning: complex sequential boosting frameworks do not automatically outperform parallel tree ensembles without extensive hyperparameter search spaces. Random Forest currently stands as the leading non-linear candidate model.

Week 3 — Part C: Feature Refinement & Decision Matrix¶

Following baseline re-evaluation and advanced model training, we perform formal Feature Refinement to document variable decisions, prevent data leakage, and optimize feature space dimensionality prior to final model selection

Feature Refinement Decision Table¶

Feature / Variable Decision Technical & Rationale Reason Expected Operational Effect
Transaction_Status Removed Target leakage risk. Post-execution status (Failed/Reversed) is unavailable at real-time pre-settlement scoring Prevents artificial model accuracy inflation and ensures realistic pre-transaction scoring in production
Customer_Tx_Count Refined Converted from global static count to chronological cumulative count (groupby.cumcount()). Eliminates temporal data leakage from future transactions into past features, stabilizing time-aware validation
customer_avg_amount Refined Computed using expanding mean with .shift(1) historical lag per customer[cite: 140]. Prevents current transaction value from contaminating historical baseline averages, reflecting true past spending habits
Is_Weekend_Transaction Corrected Adjusted condition logic from dayofweek > 5 to dayofweek >= 5 Accurately captures both Saturday (5) and Sunday (6) off-peak support risk profiles
Amount_NGN_Capped Added Upper-bound IQR capping applied to raw transaction amount (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR) Stabilizes linear coefficient fitting without removing extreme tail risk signals from high-value transfers
Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio Retained High predictive importance in tree ensembles (~5.74% Gini importance) Enhances model sensitivity to sudden individual spending spikes relative to historical account baselines

Summary Analysis of Model Trade-offs¶

  1. Risk Capture Leader (Recall):

    • Random Forest Classifier achieves the highest risk detection rate (Recall = 73.16% at threshold 0.4286), successfully intercepting 338 out of 462 high-risk events
    • From a compliance perspective, maximizing Recall minimizes unmitigated financial loss from undetected fraudulent transactions

  2. Precision & Workload Efficiency Leader:

    • Logistic Regression (Threshold = 0.57) achieves higher overall Accuracy (70.08%) and Precision (31.71%), generating fewer false alarms (478 False Positives) and reducing compliance review queue overhead

  3. PR-AUC Discrimination & F1 Balance:

    • Random Forest delivers the highest F1-Score (0.3939), balancing precision and recall effectively
    • Logistic Regression maintains a slightly higher PR-AUC (0.3360), reflecting robust probability calibration across linear feature spaces

  4. Strategic Choice for Week 4 Candidate Final Model:

    • Random Forest Classifier is selected as the candidate model to advance into Week 4 (Final Testing & Optimization) due to its superior minority class recall and F1-score, with hyperparameter tuning scheduled in Week 4 to prune false positives

Week 3 — Part E: Error Analysis (False Positives vs. False Negatives)¶

In financial risk screening, overall classification accuracy is an insufficient metric. A granular Error Analysis is critical to evaluate the operational trade-offs between two types of prediction errors:

  1. False Positives (FP) — Type I Error: Legitimate transactions incorrectly flagged for risk review. This creates customer friction (blocked transactions) and increases manual compliance review workloads
  2. False Negatives (FN) — Type II Error: Actual high-risk transactions missed by the model. This directly exposes FinTrust Digital Bank to financial losses, chargebacks, and compliance penalties

We analyze the confusion matrix and error patterns of our candidate Random Forest Classifier ($Threshold = 0.4286$).

Key Discovery & Error Pattern Analysis (Part E)¶

  1. False Negative Analysis (124 Missed Risks):

    • Financial Impact: The model missed 124 out of 462 high-risk transactions (26.84% leakage rate)
    • Root Cause Pattern: Missed risk cases primarily occurred on domestic transactions executed during standard daytime hours (Transaction_Hour between 09:00 and 17:00) with moderate amounts. Because these mimic legitimate user behavior, tree splits could not isolate them without extreme false alarm escalation

  2. False Positive Analysis (916 False Alarms):

    • Operational Impact: To achieve a high 73.16% Recall, 916 legitimate transactions were flagged for review, yielding a False Positive Rate of 47.27% on Class 0
    • Root Cause Pattern: False positives are heavily concentrated in night-time transactions (Is_Night_Transaction = 1) and first-time customer transfers where personal spending baselines (customer_avg_amount) are not yet well-established

  3. Strategic Mitigation Plan for Week 4:

    • Implement a two-tiered decision threshold: automatically approve low-score predictions, send medium-score predictions to manual review, and automatically block high-score predictions.

Week 3 — Part F: Model Interpretation & Feature Drivers¶

To ensure model transparency and explainability for financial compliance officers, we inspect the global decision drivers of our candidate Random Forest Classifier using Gini Feature Importance and Permutation Feature Importance.

Interpretation of Key Model Drivers — Permutation Importance (Part F)¶

Evaluating feature importance via Permutation Importance on the time-split test set measures the exact drop in Average Precision (PR-AUC) when each feature's values are randomly shuffled. This reveals the true empirical decision drivers of our candidate Random Forest Classifier:

1. Primary Structural Risk Drivers (Transaction_Type & Amount_NGN)¶

  • Transaction_Type (Rank #1): Permutating transaction types causes the largest performance degradation, dropping Average Precision by ~0.038. Specific operational categories represent the single most dominant structural determinant of risk flagging
  • Amount_NGN (Rank #2): Absolute monetary transaction value causes the second-largest drop in PR-AUC (~0.034). Financial exposure remains a foundational split condition for risk partitioning across decision trees

2. Secondary Temporal & Geographic Context (Transaction_Hour & International_Transaction)¶

  • Transaction_Hour & International_Transaction (Ranks #3 & #4): Permutating execution hour or cross-border status induces a ~0.0056 to ~0.0058 drop in PR-AUC. Off-peak night execution and international origin provide critical contextual signals that modulate transaction risk scores

3. Empirical Validation of Engineered Features (CrossBorder_Web_Interaction)¶

  • CrossBorder_Web_Interaction (Rank #5): The engineered interaction feature capturing international operations via Web/ATM/POS channels ranks directly in the Top 5 feature drivers (~0.0029 PR-AUC drop). This empirically validates Hypothesis $H_4$, proving that explicit cross-border channel interactions enhance the model's discriminative boundary
  • Secondary Stabilizers (Age, Amount_NGN_Capped, Digital_Engagement_Score, Amount_Category, Is_High_Value_Customer_Anomaly): Demographic and capped spending metrics provide fine-grained secondary calibration for marginal boundary predictions.

Week 3 — Part G: Candidate Final Model Selection for Week 4 Integration¶

In accordance with official project guidelines, this section formally documents the candidate model selected to carry forward into Week 4 (Final Testing, Refinement, & Integration).

Candidate Model Documentation Summary¶

  • 1. Model Selected:

    • Random Forest Classifier (Tuned Probability Threshold = 0.4286)

  • 2. Rationale for Selection:

    • Superior Risk Capture Rate (Recall = 73.16%): Outperforms Logistic Regression (48.05%), XGBoost (60.39%), and LightGBM (67.10%) in detecting minority high-risk transactions
    • Highest F1-Score Balance (0.3939): Delivers the optimal harmonic mean between precision and recall under chronological time-aware split validation
    • Robustness to Synthetic Noise: Parallel tree averaging (Bagging) handles broad synthetic feature rules more effectively than default sequential boosting

  • 3. Features Used (16 Refined Domain Features):

    • Amount_NGN, Amount_NGN_Capped, Customer_Tx_Count (Cumulative), Transaction_Frequency, Is_Unverified_Device, Location_Mismatch_Flag, Digital_Engagement_Category, Transaction_Hour, Transaction_Day, Is_Night_Transaction, Is_Weekend_Transaction (Corrected), New_Account_High_Risk, CrossBorder_Web_Interaction, Channel_Mismatch_Flag, customer_avg_amount (Leak-Free), Amount_To_Customer_Avg_Ratio.

  • 4. Preprocessing Pipeline:

    • Continuous Features: Standardized using StandardScaler()
    • Categorical Features: Encoded using OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', drop='first')
    • Outlier Treatment: Explicit IQR capping on Amount_NGN
    • Class Weighting: Balanced class weights (class_weight='balanced').

  • 5. Validation Evaluation Results (Chronological Test Set - 2,400 Records):

    • Accuracy: 56.67%
    • Precision: 26.95%
    • Recall: 73.16% (338 out of 462 risks caught)
    • F1-Score: 0.3939
    • PR-AUC: 0.3131 (Average Precision: 0.3148)

  • 6. Identified Limitations:

    • False Positive Volume: To maintain 73%+ recall, the model generates 916 false alarms, requiring compliance review capacity
    • Synthetic Target Limitations: As a synthetic educational dataset, ground-truth labels reflect predefined creation rules rather than organic real-world fraud tactics
